title: Maryland Gov. Wes Moore warns against Trump admin. hands-off AI policy
key_facts: Maryland Governor Wes Moore, speaking at the Maryland Innovation Summit in Baltimore, spoke out against the Trump administration's position that no federal legislation is needed to control AI.
He said there are 'no federal guardrails' and called the absence of federal leadership 'staggering'.
Moore said the administration avoids congressional AI controls because the technology is driving much of the US economy: without AI, 'the stock market would be down at this point'.
He warned the accord's promise could be overtaken by software running on its own with its own interests.
He called on the National Governors Association to take the lead on the digital future.
Context: Trump got big tech leaders to sign an AI accord at the White House on Wednesday that leaves control of the products to developers.
quote_evidence: "The thing we know right now is that there are no federal guardrails. We are seeing an absence of federal leadership on this issue; and that is not just concerning, it is staggering, particularly when we know how people are feeling right now," Moore said.
"If you were to disaggregate AI from the movement of equities, the stock market would be down at this point," Moore said.
why_it_matters_hint: Another Democratic governor pushes states and the governors' association to fill the federal gap on AI rules.
notes: Short local report; the summit date is not given. Follow-up of 1002:C13-09: new today is Moore's speech and his call to the National Governors Association.
